verses.text: The Lord Yahweh’s Spirit is on me; because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble. He has sent me to bind up the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
to proclaim the year of Yahweh’s favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn;

to provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.
They will rebuild the old ruins. They will raise up the places long devastated. They will repair the ruined cities, that have been devastated for many generations.
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will work your fields and your vineyards.
But you will be called Yahweh’s priests. Men will call you the servants of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will boast in their glory.
Instead of your shame you will have double. Instead of dishonor, they will rejoice in their portion. Therefore in their land, they will possess double. Everlasting joy will be to them.
“For I, Yahweh, love justice. I hate robbery and iniquity. I will give them their reward in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring  will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge them, that they are the offspring  which Yahweh has blessed.”

I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation. He has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
For as the earth produces its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring up; so the Lord Yahweh will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.

footnotes.content: Notice how the Lord's anointing is *on* the speaker, not just within—it spills out into the world. To preach good news to the humble, to bind the broken hearted: this is what happens when the Spirit comes with permission. It takes both the Spirit's work and our willingness to carry it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The year of Yahweh's favor and the day of His vengeance live in the same breath—restoration and judgment are not opposites but two sides of His truth. Both comfort the broken: judgment ends the reign of injustice, and favor begins the healing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What a reversal: ashes become a garland, mourning becomes oil of joy, heaviness becomes a garment of praise. And we don't just receive these—we become *trees* that display them, rooted and growing, the Lord's planting. Our transformation itself glorifies Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ruins are rebuilt, not by some distant miracle, but by hands and will—the people themselves. Generations of ruin did not break the thread; there is still someone to rise and repair. Desolation, however long, is not permanent.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Outsiders tending your fields—a sign of peace and trust, not conquest. When enemies become servants by choice, it speaks of a restoration so complete that even old enmities are healed. The land itself can rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From captive to priest—the entire identity shifts. Priesthood is not rank but access, a standing before Yahweh on behalf of others. And 'servants of our God' speaks both privilege and humility. To serve is to be honored; to be honored is to serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Double in exchange for shame—not just compensation but surplus, abundance that overflows the account. The text says *they* will rejoice in their *portion*, speaking to a deep contentment that springs from justice, not hunger.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord *loves* justice and *hates* robbery—His character is stated plainly. And His reward is given *in truth*, meaning not merely in fact but in a way that aligns with what is real and right. The covenant that follows is not a transaction but a binding of Himself to His word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The offspring become the proof—known, acknowledged, blessed visibly. You cannot hide a blessing that fruitful; it speaks for itself across nations. To be blessed is to be recognizable, to carry the marks of the Lord's hand in a way others can see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The speaker's joy is personal, intimate—my soul, my God—yet dressed in images of covenant ceremony: the bride adorned, the bridegroom decked. Salvation is both the closest comfort and the grandest celebration, wrapping us in righteousness like festive clothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: the Lord causes righteousness to spring up *before all nations*, visible and growing as a garden grows—not in secret, but openly. We see it still, quietly, wherever broken things are tended back to wholeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
